newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso gains, helped by C Bank rate.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso gains, helped by C Bank rate.

text.p: The Philippine peso gained on Tuesday as banks lightened their holdings in view of the Central Bank's still high overnight borrowing rate of 15 percent, traders said.
Some arbitrage money also came in to re-establish positions to take advantage of the high overnight rate.
The peso settled at 26.374 to the dollar from the previous 26.376. Volume was lower at $204.5 million from $459.85 million.
Traders said the Central Bank sold about $53 million in the morning at the rates of 26.372 for delivery today and at 26.377 for settlement the next day.
Banks had bought dollars from the Central Bank after Monday's hefty demand when banks closed their positions for the first half.
"By afternoon, those who bought dollars eventually sold," a foreign bank dealer said. "They saw that the exchange rate was stable. There was no need to panic."
The Central Bank was estimated to have bought $31 million in the afternnon at the rates of 26.376 and 26.375.
Traders said they expected the peso to remain stable on Wednesday with the Central Bank keeping its key rate at 15 percent.
